Packed red earth worn bare by generations of display, a rough circle of scrapes edged by a wall of tree-ferns three metres tall, amber afternoon light flooding the floor, the surrounding fronds trembling at the slightest footfall.

A wide river sandbar of pale amber shingle, water running fast on both sides, the far bank terraced in red clay and dark araucaria, the wet gravel gleaming under a white midday sky that fills the entire overhead.

A fern clearing twenty metres across, the canopy gap letting four hard columns of gold light fall onto deep green moss, the enclosing horsetail stems rising to shoulder height on every side, the floor spongy and yielding underfoot.

A volcanic ash flat banded in sulphur-yellow and rust-orange, shallow steam rising from three fissures along the eastern edge, the crust firm but hollow-sounding, a semicircle of dark basalt boulders on the far side making a natural backstop.

A bloom-covered meadow at full flower, magenta and deep orange to every horizon, seed-heads brushing at knee height, the whole field enclosed to the north by a low ridge of cycad palms that cuts the sky into a flat green line.

A tidal mudflat at dead low water, the cracked grey surface holding a sky of bruised violet cloud as a perfect unbroken mirror, a dense fringe of horsetails ringing the back edge, the air smelling of salt and warm sulphur.

A lakeshore of black volcanic sand, the water gone glass-still in the windless morning, a dense curtain of reeds three metres tall on three sides, a single enormous tree-fern arching over the display floor and dropping its shadow in a clean half-circle.

A rock amphitheatre, tiered sandstone benches rising in rough steps around a flat orange stage floor, iron-red streaks running vertically down the back wall, the stone hot to the touch and still radiating last night's heat into the cool dawn air.

A forest gap where a fallen araucaria sixty metres long has cleared the canopy, the enormous pale trunk itself a raised stage, the raw wound in the forest floor churned to orange clay, light falling in a single uninterrupted shaft from the gap above.

A high saddle between two ridges, cloud streaming through below in a slow white river, the ground a thin wet turf of low club-moss, the enclosing ridge-lines on both sides dark with silhouetted cycads, the air cold and bright.

A lek worn bare through countless seasons, the earth packed to the hardness of fired clay, a ring of shallow scrapes and drag-marks defining a rough circle, the surrounding tree-ferns leaning inward, one enormous drift of shed fronds piled golden in the hollow behind.

A river sandbar of cream-coloured silt, the channel braiding around both edges in shallow amber water, the far bank rising in three distinct clay terraces of orange, buff, and deep red, a single cycad standing at the apex of the tallest terrace.

A fern clearing where the ground is a carpet of unbroken bright-green moss, four columns of hard afternoon light angling in from the south-west, the clearing edged by a dense stand of giant horsetails whose ribbed stems catch the light in vertical lines.

An ash flat where the crust has banded into concentric rings of cream, pale green, and deep rust around each vent, steam rising from a long diagonal fissure, the flat surrounded on three sides by a low collar of dark welded tuff.

A meadow in full bloom, deep yellow and violet flowers to the horizon on the open side, a curved bank of low cycads closing the northern edge, the ground cover so thick and soft that each step leaves a clear pressed print for hours.

A tidal mudflat whose cracked grey surface reflects a sky of hard copper at late afternoon, a reef of dark grey mudstone running along the back edge like a natural wall, the surface firm at the centre, softening to dark wet clay near the water.

A lakeshore where cream-coloured sand meets utterly still dark water, a wall of tall reeds standing unmoved on the far margin, one massive araucaria trunk fallen half into the lake, its surface bleached silver and serving as a raised walkway to the display floor.

A sandstone amphitheatre whose tiered walls are stained deep red by iron-rich seeps, the flat floor covered in a thin skin of orange grit, one wide crack in the back wall holding a colony of small cycads that overflow down the stone like water.

A forest gap opened by two fallen giants side by side, their trunks forming parallel walls on opposite edges of a long narrow stage, the floor stripped to raw red clay by the impact, a column of bright sky visible overhead the full length of the gap.

A high saddle where the ground underfoot is deep purple-brown peat moss, both flanks dropping away into cloud, a line of wind-twisted araucaria standing along the eastern ridge like a broken comb, the cloud below lit gold by a low sun.

A lek of deep red packed earth, the display ring surrounded by a dense crescent of tree-ferns whose fronds form a continuous green canopy at four metres, a single large scrape in the centre holding a pool of rainwater the colour of strong tea.

A shingle spit of dark grey gravel curving into still water on both sides, the distant bank rising in pale horizontal layers of limestone and dark clay, the wet shingle catching the light in a thousand small glints, the air carrying the smell of green water.

A fern clearing whose floor is a solid mat of bright emerald ground-fern, the canopy gap nearly circular, the enclosing forest rising to thirty metres on every side, late light coming in at a low angle and catching the spore-haze lifting from the disturbed fronds.

A volcanic ash flat where steam vents from a long curved fissure, the crust around it banded in vivid bands of chrome-yellow, pale grey, and deep brick-red, the surrounding plain ringed by a low escarpment of dark basalt that traps the warm air close to the ground.

A bloom meadow where the flowers run from copper-orange at the edges to deep crimson at the centre, seed-heads at knee height throughout, the meadow bowl enclosed on all sides by a curving bank of tree-ferns whose fronds droop inward over the top of the display floor.

A lek worn to orange clay by seasons of use, the earth cracked in a rough circle where feet have churned it bare, a stockade of horsetails eight meters tall closing the edge, and one deep scrape at the center still damp from morning rain

A river sandbar of pale shingle, water running bronze on both sides, the far bank rising in red-clay terraces stacked like rough shelves, the gravel underfoot clicking and shifting, the whole spit long enough to hold a crowd and narrow enough to feel surrounded

A fern clearing where three araucaria have shed their canopy and hard columns of noon light fall straight to the ground, the ferns beaten low by previous gatherings, the soil dark and spongy, the living wall of fronds bright chartreuse at the lit edge

A volcanic ash flat pale as bone, the crust banded in rust and sulphur-yellow toward the fissures, steam rising in slow curls from a crack that runs the length of the arena, the ground firm at the margin but chalking underfoot at the center

A bloom-covered meadow running to every horizon under a wide copper sky, the display ground a natural hollow where seed-heads reach shoulder height and the petals are a saturated violet so dense it reads almost black in the shade of each other

A tidal mudflat at low water, the surface a perfect mirror throwing back a mackerel sky in silver and rose, the mud firm enough to hold weight, the far edge of the flat dissolving into a wall of dark mangrove root that closes the seaward side

A lakeshore where the water has gone still as poured tin, reeds at the margin forming a dense bronze colonnade, the packed sand underfoot white and fine, a single cycad fallen years ago now half buried and serving as an accidental central marker

A rock amphitheatre, a natural bowl of dark basalt in tiered rings worn smooth by weather, the stage floor a circle of pale grit between the tiers, and a diagonal crack in the back wall from which a cycad grows, its crown catching the only direct sun

A forest gap where the largest araucaria on the ridge came down in the last wet season, its trunk a full two meters across lying moss-dark and enormous, the gap it tore now flooded with hard equatorial light, the exposed soil red and churned

A high saddle between two ridges, the ground a thin mat of moss over cold rock, cloud pouring through the gap below in a slow river of white, the flanking ridges closing the view to either side into dark walls of conifer and cycad

A lek worn to raw red earth, the scrapes arranged in an uneven ring around a central depression, the surrounding horsetails tall and dark green making a closed wall, the soil dry and powdery at the surface, rising in small red clouds at each footfall

A river sandbar of silver-white gravel, the two channels catching different light, one amber and one pale green, the gravel coarse underfoot, the far bank a vertical red-clay wall draped with hanging fern fronds reaching almost to the waterline

A fern clearing in tall forest, the canopy gap an oval of burning blue above, the light coming down in four distinct columns that move slowly as the day turns, the ground a deep mat of broken frond and dark soil, the enclosing wall of tree ferns unbroken

A volcanic ash flat at the foot of a low cone, the ground banded in alternating rings of white ash and orange iron crust, a single vent near the north edge producing a continuous plume of white steam that drifts south and catches the low sun gold

A bloom-covered meadow at peak flower, the display site a natural round depression lower than the surrounding stems, the petals around it in three distinct bands of yellow, orange, and a deep arterial red, seed-heads nodding in the warm updraft from the open ground

A tidal mudflat so flat and still that the standing animals cast doubled shadows, one below and one reflected, the mud surface iridescent where thin water still films it, the enclosing edge a dense dark wall of coastal cycad and pneumatophore root

A lakeshore at dusk, the water still and dark as iron, reeds forming a semicircle thirty meters across, the packed wet sand underfoot leaving clear impressions, a raft of pink flowering aquatic plants at the margin providing the only saturated colour in the grey-gold evening

A rock amphitheatre of pale limestone, the tiers stained orange and green by lichen, the floor of white fractured stone level and broad, a thin sheet of water from a seep crossing one corner and catching light like a blade, the whole bowl holding sound

A forest gap cleared by a fallen giant, the trunk itself serving as the upstage wall, bark lifting in orange and brown plates, a strip of red earth churned between the trunk and the surrounding living trees, resurrection ferns already greening the exposed wood

A high saddle under a fast-moving sky, the mossy ground wet and spongy, a low wall of wind-sheared cycads on either side, the cloud river below the saddle catching the afternoon sun from beneath and glowing copper, the ridge behind rising dark and close

A lek of pale grey clay beaten flat, surrounded by a thicket of giant horsetails whose segmented green columns reach four times standing height, a shallow puddle left at the center by last night's rain, already printing with the first returning feet

A river sandbar where the main channel has deposited a long arc of black volcanic sand between two pale shingle banks, the black strip warm underfoot and striking, the far bank showing red clay above and a dense fringe of horsetail below

A fern clearing where the soil is deep rust-red and the enclosing tree ferns are so tall their fronds close over part of the gap, the light falling in one wide column at an angle, throwing half the floor into warm amber and half into blue shadow

A volcanic ash flat edged on three sides by a low escarpment of dark basalt, the flat itself pale grey with sulphur-yellow seams, steam rising from two fissures simultaneously, the steam plumes crossing above the center of the arena before dispersing

A bloom-covered meadow where the flowers are white with purple centers and run unbroken to a low ridge of dark cycad scrub, the display hollow pressed into the slope, the stems around it leaning inward at the edge, seed-heads brushing anyone who passes

A tidal mudflat at the lowest of the tide, the surface cracked into large pale polygons rimmed in dark wet mud, a mirror of standing water collecting in the lower polygons, the enclosing wall of coastal forest a dense dark line on three sides

A lakeshore with reeds in full plume, the reed heads silver against a dark green background, the sand hard-packed and pale at the water's edge, a single large driftwood log half buried in the margin, smoothed and dark, the water behind it perfectly still

A rock amphitheatre carved by a now-dry waterfall, the curved back wall stained in orange and black mineral streaks, the floor smooth and level with fine gravel over stone, a fringe of small cycads growing from cracks in the lower tier, fronds catching the lateral light

A forest gap where three trees fell in sequence creating a long corridor of light, the stage floor a strip of dark peaty soil, the trunks lying parallel on either side making natural enclosing walls, bracket fungi bright orange along the nearest one

A lek worn to bare red clay on a slight rise, the ring of scrapes visible as a lighter circle inside the bare patch, a grove of cycads with vivid orange seed-cones forming the enclosing edge to the south, the clay dry and fine and rising at each step

A fern clearing where last season's burn has left the soil black and the new fronds are pushing up electric green at knee height, the clearing edge a sharp boundary where the old unburned tree ferns stand dark and dense, the contrast between black ground and bright frond absolute

A river sandbar of pale cream shingle, water rushing on both sides, the far bank striped red and ochre in layered clay, a single enormous driftwood log anchoring the upstream end where the gravel runs slick and wet.

A fern clearing ringed by araucaria trunks rising forty metres, hard columns of amber morning light falling through the canopy gap onto a floor of bright green fronds already flattened in a rough display oval by repeated use.

A lek worn to bare packed earth, the colour of old brick, a ring of shallow scrapes pressed into the surface, surrounding vegetation beaten back to a rough circle of exposed soil where generations of feet have turned the ground to dust.

A bloom-covered meadow at absolute peak flower, magenta and gold to every horizon, seed-heads swaying at knee height, the ground beneath a dense mat of petals and soft stem, a distant ridge of cycad forest closing the far edge in dark green.

A rock amphitheatre of tiered pale limestone, the bowl curving in natural steps down to a flat stone floor worn smooth, a cascade of maidenhair fern spilling over the upper tier in a single bright green curtain, the stone underfoot dusted with dry mineral chalk.

A forest gap where a colossal araucaria has fallen, the trunk itself a stage thirty metres long and two metres across, bark orange-red in the direct sun, the ground around it churned to dark soft loam, the standing canopy enclosing the gap on every side.

A lakeshore at first light, the water gone absolutely still, a broad margin of dark wet sand between the water and the reed wall, the reeds forming a solid ochre enclosure, a single rotting log at the water's edge hosting a bright cap of orange shelf fungi.

A fern clearing where a giant tree fern has collapsed at the centre, its crown spreading across the ground in a mat of bronze fronds, columns of white midday light driving down through the canopy gap, the clearing floor uneven with root humps and bright moss.

A river sandbar at a sharp bend, grey-white shingle packed firm and wet underfoot, the near channel running shallow and fast, the far bank rising in five distinct horizontal strata of red, purple, cream, rust, and grey, the bend enclosing the bar on three sides.

A lek of exposed pale clay, beaten into a hard oval by many seasons, the surrounding horsetails standing three metres tall in an unbroken green palisade, the individual scrapes within the ring still holding last night's rain in shallow copper-coloured puddles.

A high saddle where the cloud pours continuously over the western ridge and dissolves in the warmer air above the stage, the ground a close-grazed mat of club moss and small fern, the twin ridges of dark green forest on both flanks drawing the eye to the open sky ahead.

A tidal mudflat with the tide out far, the cracked surface forming irregular grey-brown tiles, a shallow residual pool at the centre catching the sky in a perfect orange rectangle at sunset, the enclosing shoreline a dense dark wall of horsetails and low cycad.

A rock amphitheatre where the limestone tiers have been stained deep amber and rust by centuries of iron seep, the stage floor a flat oval of pale gravel, a thin rivulet crossing the back of the arena and disappearing into a cleft in the rock, leaving the stones around it bright green with algae.

A lakeshore where the water has dropped to expose a broad shelf of dark wet silt, reeds standing in a dense ochre wall behind, the open lake ahead catching the afternoon light, the silt underfoot dense and giving, holding each footprint as a deep clean impression.

A river sandbar of fine orange-gold sand deposited at a confluence, two channels framing it on either side, the far bank a sheer cut-face of dark compressed clay with thin roots hanging free, the sand underfoot still damp and firm from the last high water.

A lek worn through successive seasons, the central earth now pale and powdery as ash, the ring of scrapes radiating outward like a rough star, surrounding vegetation bent back into a low hedge of cycad frond and horsetail, the whole arena lit by raking late-afternoon sun that catches every raised rim of every scrape.

A high saddle in cloud, the ground a wet black peat over stone, small bright pools reflecting white sky between mats of vivid green sphagnum, the ridges on both sides dense with low araucaria bent by prevailing wind, and a single enormous erratic boulder at the saddle's centre serving as an unmistakable marker.

A bloom-covered meadow at the end of the dry season, the flowers past their peak and the seed-heads dense and heavy, the ground below a springy compressed mat of stem and dry petal, the arena enclosed by a horseshoe of tall cycad and cycadeoid, their crowns backlit gold.

A tidal mudflat at the lowest tide of the season, the mirror surface broken only by the raised trails left by overnight invertebrates, the enclosing mangrove wall behind in deep shade, and a thin bright line of sea at the far horizon making the flat feel suspended between two skies.

A rock amphitheatre of dark basalt with white mineral streaks running diagonally across the tiers like enormous brushstrokes, the stage floor a flat oval of fine dark gravel, a shallow rainwater pool in the centre reflecting the surrounding rock walls in miniature detail.

A lakeshore where the reed margin has been broken and trampled into a rough semicircle, the broken reeds forming a low pale wall, the exposed lakebed within a firm dark silt, the open water beyond perfectly still and carrying a doubled image of the far forested shore in reversed green and grey.

A forest gap where the fallen trunk has already begun to return to the earth, its top surface covered in a continuous sheet of bright orange bracket fungi, the gap floor around it a dark churned earth of root fragments and moss, tree-fern trunks enclosing every side in a tight dark colonnade.

A lek on a broad river terrace above the floodplain, the display earth packed to a smooth pale hardness, the scrape-ring surrounding it pressed deep by many seasons, the far edge of the terrace dropping away in a red clay bluff above the river, giving the arena an open horizon on one side and a dense cycad hedge on the other three.

A high saddle where the cloud-river pours over the western ridge in a slow continuous cascade and pools briefly in the saddle hollow before dissolving, the ground below it a close wet turf of moss over bedrock, the twin flanking ridges of dark araucaria forest rising steeply on both sides into the cloud above.

A lek worn to bare packed clay, the earth orange-red and polished by countless seasons, a rough ring of scrapes visible at the margin, the surrounding cycad scrub beaten back into a ragged green wall, every stalk bent outward.

A bloom meadow running wall to wall with waist-high magenta flowers, the seed-heads already trembling with wind, the whole thing cupped between two low ridges of pale sandstone, one hollow at the centre holding a drift of fallen petals in a deep pink pile.

A fallen giant, its trunk six metres across and mossy along the top, spanning a forest gap floored with new ferns, the surrounding trees pressing close on both sides, amber afternoon light coming in at one end like a spotlight on the log's flat crown.

A rock amphitheatre of tiered grey limestone, each ledge just wide enough for an animal to stand, the stage floor below of pale sandy grit scattered with dark pebbles, a single column of red stone standing at the back like a marker placed there deliberately.

A lakeshore where the water has gone glass-still at evening, soft mud at the margin printed deeply by every visitor, reeds dense and golden at the far edge, a bank of tree ferns curving around the back, their fronds forming a continuous green canopy overhead.

A river sandbar mid-channel, shingle white as bone underfoot, the current braiding fast on the east side and slow and copper on the west, a bleached log grounded at the bar's narrow upstream tip forming a natural backstop to the whole stage.

A lek on packed red earth surrounded by a dense wall of horsetails three metres tall, the stems so close together they form a solid green enclosure, the scrape ring in the centre showing paler subsoil, the whole floor smelling of churned wet clay.

A bloom meadow at full colour, blue-purple to the treeline on three sides, the fourth side a sandstone bluff dropping the light in late afternoon like a wall of amber, seed-heads at knee height and a bowl-shaped low point at the centre where the flowers grow tallest.

A lakeshore with a basalt headland curving around three sides like a cupped hand, still water on the open fourth side, the margin mud deep black and printed wall to wall with tracks, a solitary cycad growing at the headland's tip throwing a shadow straight across the stage floor.

A rock amphitheatre cut by a seasonal stream now dry, the streambed floor packed white gravel, tiers of red sandstone rising on three sides in natural ledges, a thin dark stripe of iron oxide running horizontally around the bowl at mid-height like a painted line.

A lek floor of packed clay, deep rust-orange, ringed by waist-high cycads whose fronds overhang the scrape like a rough colonnade, one split frond fallen across the edge and slowly browning in the heat.
A fern clearing under araucaria giants, hard columns of noon light driving down through the canopy gap onto a floor of chest-deep fern that the display has churned to bright green pulp at the centre.

A bloom-covered meadow running to the horizon in dense copper-gold and violet, the display floor beaten to bare dark soil at the centre, seed-heads nodding at knee height around the clearing's edge in every direction.

A lakeshore stage of coarse black sand where the water has gone glassy, a dense reed-bed curving around the back of the clearing, one enormous lily pad stranded at the margin where the water line retreated overnight.

A natural rock amphitheatre, its tiered sandstone walls the colour of dried blood, the flat stage floor a mosaic of grey lichenous stone and rust-red grit, a thin waterfall threading silently down the far wall into nothing.

A forest-gap stage built on the trunk of a fallen araucaria sixty metres long, its bark split and brick-red, the canopy walls closing on three sides, a shaft of gold light falling precisely across the centre of the log.

A lek of deep burnt-umber earth, the scrape ring widened over generations to hold a dozen animals, horsetail stems broken at the perimeter and slowly silvering, the air above the clearing thick with seed-down and copper morning light.

A shingle spit pushing into a wide slow river, the rounded grey stones wet and ringing underfoot where the display churns them, the far bank a sheer wall of layered green-grey marl, and between them the water holds a perfect upside-down sky.

A meadow clearing at peak flower in saturated crimson and yellow, the surrounding tree-fern arcade bending inward on heavy fronds, the display floor compressed to a dark oval of pressed petals and damp earth at the clearing's heart.

A dry riverbed of exposed pale sandstone, the bedrock scoured flat and smooth by seasonal floods and warm underfoot in the afternoon sun, a fringe of dense horsetail crowding both cut banks above, the channel curving gently so that both ends of the stage disappear behind green walls and the arena feels entirely enclosed.
